title: Noah’s Ark
subtitle: Explore Noah’s camp, gather supplies, and help build the ark.
releaseNote: Noah’s Ark · explore, gather, and build the ark

content.objective: Find Noah, inspect the ark, gather supplies, then help Noah build the ark.
content.bible: God instructed Noah to make an ark from gopher wood and cover it with pitch inside and outside. Genesis gives its dimensions as 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high. The passage also describes a roof, a door in the side, and three decks. This is a summary; read Genesis 6:13–16 in your Bible.
noah: Aaron! Glad you made it. I have a lot of work ahead of me. Would you help me gather some supplies?
We'll need three pieces of wood, two coils of rope, and my hammer — and that jar of pitch by the stream, for sealing the ark. One piece of wood may be tucked behind that fallen log.
ark: The ark is enormous, isn't it? Come closer to the ramp and take a look.
God gave Noah detailed instructions for the ark. You can read about them in Genesis 6.
discovery: You found a quiet place beside the stream. The whole adventure begins with listening and looking closely.
before_noah: The ark is still being prepared. Find Noah in the clearing; he can tell you more about the work.
inspect_first: The ark is an amazing sight. Walk up to the ramp and take a closer look before gathering materials.
after_talk: Thanks for helping, Aaron. Take your time exploring. I’ll be right here when you’re ready to show me what you found.
materials_complete: That's everything — wood, rope, hammer, and even the pitch! Bring them back to Noah.
return_noah: Great work, Aaron! The supplies are all here. That should help us get ready to build.
build_start: That's everything, Aaron — supplies, tools, and pitch. Now comes the best part.
God gave me the plan: strong ribs, three decks, a door in the side, and pitch inside and out. Will you help me build it? The plan is waiting up by the ark.
build_locked: The plan is ready, but building can't start until all the supplies are at the building site: the wood, rope, my hammer, and the jar of pitch by the stream.
pitch_reminder: Almost ready to build — I still need that jar of pitch by the stream. We can't seal the ark without it.
build_progress: The ark is taking shape, Aaron. Ribs first, then the decks, then pitch and the door — one stage at a time. The plan by the ark shows what's next.
ark_finished: There it stands — finished, sealed, and ready. One day God will send the animals, two by two.
For now, the ark waits. There will be more of this story to explore.
blueprint_clue: I found the plan beside the ark. Genesis says to use gopher wood and cover the ark with pitch inside and outside.
The ark was 300 cubits long, 50 wide, and 30 high. It had a roof, a door in the side, and three decks. Let’s study the shape of the plan together.
blueprint_finished: You restored the keel and arranged all three decks. Genesis 6:14–16 records the instructions God gave Noah.
complete: You did it, Aaron! The ark stands finished — ribs, three decks, a door, a window, and pitch on every seam, just as God described.
You earned the Noah character card. God kept His promise to Noah — and this is only the beginning of the story.

discovery_build.title: God gave Noah the plan
discovery_build.verse: God told Noah: make the ark from gopher wood, cover it inside and out with pitch, put a roof on it and a door in its side, and build three decks — lower, second, and third. (Genesis 6:14–16, summarized)
discovery_build.observation: God didn't just say “build a boat.” He gave Noah the wood, the covering, the door, the window, and three decks. God cares about the details — and Noah trusted Him before he had seen a single drop of rain.
discovery_build.question: Noah kept building for a long time before the flood came. What is something you can keep doing faithfully, even when it's hard to see why yet?

mystery_invite: The outside is finished — but step inside, Aaron. The inside is still a mystery.
I know the ark needs nine rooms across its three decks, and I have notes and diagrams scattered everywhere. What I don't have is the finished plan.
Come in and help me work out where everything belongs.
mystery_intro: Here it is: three decks, and nine rooms to place — birds, sheep, large animals, food, water, tools, the workshop, our family's quarters, and supplies.
My planning diagram is unfinished. But the ark itself remembers the plan: there are notes, labels and diagrams all over these decks, if you look carefully.
Explore every deck. When you find a clue, it will be added to the blueprint on my planning table. Then reason out where each room belongs.
And Aaron — I will not simply mark your work. A plan you only guessed is no plan at all.
mystery_status: You have found {found} of the clues hidden in the ark. Keep exploring all three decks — some clues need a little work to uncover.
When you are ready, open the blueprint and start placing rooms. Use pencil marks for the maybes.
mystery_final: Every condition holds? Wonderful. Then one last check before we build the rooms — the most important one, from a father's point of view.
One last thing: the living quarters must not be directly above the workshop. My family will never sleep with hammering underneath them!
Check the plan against that, and then submit it. If it passes, we build exactly what you have drawn.
mystery_congrats: It passes. Every clue, and my final check too — this is a plan that works, Aaron.
You did not guess your way here. You explored, you gathered the evidence, and you reasoned. That is how good builders work.
Master Architect of the ark — your grandfather would be proud. Now, shall we see about some animals?
mystery_done: The rooms are being built to your plan, Master Architect. The animals will be arriving soon — that is the next great work.

reflection_mystery.title: God's Instructions, Noah's Faith
reflection_mystery.verse: Noah did this; he did all that God commanded him. — Genesis 6:22
lessons: God gave Noah specific instructions for building the ark — its size, its wood, its three decks (Genesis 6:14–16).
Noah obeyed what God commanded, carefully and completely, even before he could see the flood.
Through the ark, God provided a means of preservation through the coming judgment.
reflection_mystery.fictionNote: The Bible tells us the ark had three decks, but it does not describe this nine-room layout. The room arrangement, the scattered clues and Aaron's investigation are fictional gameplay — the faithfulness is Noah's.

flood_invite: Aaron. The animals are coming to the ark two by two, just as God commanded — but look at the sky over the valley.
The rain is coming: the very flood God warned me about. The way back from the grazing valley crosses low ground, and the waters will rise fast.
Cross the valley while there is time. Read the water, use the high ground, and plan every crossing before you take it. On the far side you will see the ark — and you will see who shuts its door.
flood_done: You saw it with your own eyes, Aaron: I did not shut the door of the ark. God shut it — and He always keeps what He promises.
dove_invite: Aaron, look — the mountaintops are appearing above the water. God made a wind pass over the earth, and the flood is going down.
But is the ground dry enough for us to leave the ark? I will send out a dove to see. A dove cannot rest on water — if it finds no resting place, it will come back to us.
You have quick eyes. Guide the dove for me: watch the wind, plan the way back, and do not let it tire. Are you ready?
dove_flight1_briefing: First flight. Fly out over the water and look for any sign that the land is coming back — branches floating, a ridge near the surface, anything.
Find two signs, then bring the dove home to the ark. Remember: a dove that finds no resting place must return, or it will tire over the endless water.
dove_flight1_return: The dove came back to Noah, because the water still covered the whole earth — it found no resting place for its feet.
So Noah reached out his hand and took the dove back into the ark. We wait, Aaron. God has not forgotten us.
dove_seven_days_1: Then he sent the dove out again — this time, it might come back with news.
dove_flight2_briefing: Second flight. Somewhere to the east, the tops of the trees are out of the water. If the dove finds an olive tree, it will bring back a leaf.
The olive tree has silver-green leaves and a split, pale trunk. Dark trees are not it — do not be fooled.
dove_flight2_return: Towards evening the dove returned — and look! A freshly plucked olive leaf in its beak!
Then Noah knew the waters had gone down from the earth. The land is coming back to life.
dove_seven_days_2: Noah waited seven more days. The ark was quiet, and everyone watched the window.
Then he sent the dove out for the third time.
dove_flight3_briefing: Third flight — and this one is different. This time, dove, find a green grove and stay there. Do not come back to the ark.
If the land is truly alive again, the dove will not return. That silence will be the best news of all.
dove_flight3_landing: The dove settled on a branch in the green grove — and did not return to the ark.
The earth was drying. A new beginning had come.
dove_wait_for_command: But Noah did not rush out. The dove was gone and the ground was drying — still he waited inside the ark.
He would not leave until God Himself told him to. Noah had learned to wait for God's word, not just for good news.
dove_leave_ark: Then God spoke to Noah: “Come out of the ark, you and your family — and bring out every living thing with you, so they can fill the earth.”
So Noah came out, with his wife, his sons and their wives — and every animal and bird came out of the ark into the new world.
dove_offering: Noah's first act in the new world was not to build a house. He built an altar, and worshiped the LORD.
And God promised in His heart: never again would a flood destroy all life on the earth.
dove_covenant: God blessed Noah and his sons, and made a covenant — with them, with their descendants, and with every living creature.
“I have set my rainbow in the clouds,” God said, “and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.”
Whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, God remembers His promise. And so do we.
dove_done: The ark is empty, and Noah has worshiped God. You guided the dove well, Aaron — and you learned to wait with Noah.
The story continues in the sunlit valley. The dove's journey is complete; its rewards are saved.
prism_invite: Noah and the living creatures have left the ark, and Noah has worshiped God. Come explore an imagined light garden in the sunlit valley.

This light garden is an imagined learning activity. Genesis does not describe Aaron or these optical devices. The puzzle will help us observe simple paths of light; it does not make God's covenant sign.
prism_opening: The rain has passed, and sunlight is returning to the valley. This light garden is an imagined learning activity. Genesis does not describe Aaron or these optical devices.
Guide the white light through mirrors, a clear prism, and mist. This puzzle can explore color, but it cannot create God's covenant sign.
prism_stage1_intro: Find the Light. Turn the two water-polished mirrors to guide the bright path around the stone wall and into the mist. Select a mirror, then choose Rotate.
prism_stage1_done: The light found its way around the wall. Next, the prism will split white light into three gameplay color groups.
prism_stage2_intro: Three Color Groups. The clear prism sends red, green, and blue paths in different directions. Charge each receiver; a charged receiver stays lit while you move the shared mirror and blocker.
prism_stage2_done: Each color group reached its receiver. The last board links light paths to shutters, so the paths must work together at the same time.
prism_stage3_intro: The Rainbow Bridge. Place the control mirror to light the upper receiver. Its relay opens the first shutter; green light then powers the second shutter while red, green, and blue mist zones stay lit together.
prism_stage3_done: All three mist zones are lit at once. The small spectrum belongs only to this imagined puzzle. The covenant sign in the biblical story is God's action, in a separate scene.
content.prism_science_note: This puzzle simplifies light into paths on a grid and three gameplay color groups. It treats mirrors as right-angle turns and a clear prism as a device that separates the paths; real light behaves in more detailed ways. Real rainbows form when sunlight is refracted as it enters water droplets, internally reflected inside them, and dispersed into colors as it leaves. The game’s red, green, and blue channels are useful for planning the puzzle, but they are not a complete model of the colors in a real rainbow.
prism_return_to_noah: Let’s leave the imagined light garden and return to Noah, who has already left the ark and worshiped God.
prism_covenant: God made a covenant with Noah, his descendants, and every living creature. God said that never again would a flood destroy all life on the earth.
God appointed the rainbow in the clouds as the sign of this covenant. Noah did not make the promise happen; God began it and gave its sign. (Genesis 9:8–17, summarized)

prism_reflection.title: A Promise That Endures
truths: God initiates the covenant with Noah, Noah’s descendants, and every living creature.
God is faithful to his word.
The rainbow is God’s appointed sign that never again will a flood destroy all flesh. This promise does not mean local floods never occur.
prism_reflection.question: Why is it important that the promise comes from God rather than from something Noah accomplished?
prism_reflection.science: Science describes how sunlight and water droplets can produce a rainbow. Genesis gives the rainbow covenant meaning as the sign God appoints.

prism_done: God's covenant with Noah and every living creature is the heart of this chapter. You can revisit the reflection or explore the imagined light puzzles again.
